clue.text: It is restricting a beginner, holding back strategy of choice range

indicators.note: the last two letters of the frame hold the next piece between them
the words it is hem in what follows, so they are written round it

parts.note: taken as written, as the two-word frame
L is the learner plate letter, a beginner

indicators.note: back tells us the strategy is read from right to left

parts.note: the strategy you choose first is your Plan A

explanation.surface: A sentence about a cautious approach that keeps a novice back from someone's favoured strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'restricting' and 'holding' both work on the frame 'It is', and 'back' turns the strategy round before it goes in. 'range' looks like choice, but it means mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain chain across northern Italy, bordering France, Switzerland and Austria, is a range.

clue.text: Get more friendly women to support Henry in Cheers

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath the rest
Henry's letter goes inside the word for thanks

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Women prop up Henry in a bar named Cheers, getting more sociable.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers was a US sitcom set in a bar, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, melting or warming up describes someone becoming less reserved toward others.

clue.text: Looking up a sun-drenched country

indicators.note: in a down answer, looking up means reading from bottom to top
the sun drenches the letter a, holding it within

parts.note: Sol is the sun, from the Latin

explanation.surface: Things are improving in a hot, sunny country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drenched' puts A inside SOL to give SOAL, which 'Looking up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked nation in Southeast Asia, bordering Vietnam and Thailand, capital Vientiane.

clue.text: A coarse City supporter, leading advocate of freedom in speech

indicators.note: the supporter goes in front of the words for coarse and city

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
ham means crude and overdone, as in ham acting; the city is the cathedral city in England's East Midlands, county town of its shire

explanation.surface: A crude football fan of some City club backs free speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City supporter' suggests a football fan, but the city is the English cathedral city and the supporter a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth US president's Gettysburg Address spoke of a new birth of freedom, and he championed the emancipation of slaves.

clue.text: This side's Dutch courage and strength typified him

definitions.meaning: a football team from Amsterdam, a famous Dutch club
a Greek warrior at Troy, renowned for great bravery and physical power

explanation.surface: A team whose Dutch courage and strength made one player its model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch courage' is bravery from drink, but it must be split: 'Dutch' ends the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Amsterdam football club and to the mighty Greek hero of Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Coming across to dim the light

definitions.text: Coming across to dim the light

parts.words: Coming across to dim the light
parts.note: describes the moon passing in front of the sun and blocking only part of its light

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming across' reads as seeming or appearing, but it is the moon literally moving across the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: In this kind of solar event the moon covers only some of the sun's disc, reducing daylight.

clue.text: Seasonal fare — trying borscht on us or 'Boston crush' cocktail?

indicators.note: trying the soup out on us means playing with its letters

explanation.surface: A cook tests beetroot soup on guests, or mixes a drink called the Boston crush.
explanation.walkthrough: A second anagram follows: 'Boston crush', signalled by 'cocktail', also makes the answer, so either half gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: These spiced, cross-marked buns are eaten at Easter, so they are food of one particular season.

clue.text: Singers of The Red Flag bass — and what we sang in the song

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the word for song

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad
B is the abbreviation for bass in music
the portion we sang is our part

explanation.surface: A choir recalls the bass line and the part they sang in a socialist anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Flag is the socialist anthem traditionally sung at the close of the conference of Britain's main left-wing party.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Britain's main left-wing political party traditionally sing The Red Flag at their annual conference.

clue.text: Cross Cajun writer?

parts.note: a zo (also dzo or zho) is the cross between a yak and a cow
Cajuns live in Louisiana, whose postal abbreviation is LA

explanation.surface: An angry Louisiana author, someone who writes in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry but is the noun: a hybrid animal. The question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist of the Rougon-Macquart cycle, who wrote J'accuse, is one example of a writer.

clue.text: Cab-drivers ultimately to have to do French 'Knowledge'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word cab-drivers

parts.note: the French verb meaning to have is avoir (French is shared by both verbs)
the French verb meaning to do or make is faire

explanation.surface: London cabbies must master the Knowledge, the street-map test, here in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The Knowledge is the exam on London streets that black-cab drivers must pass, which steers the solver toward taxis rather than French verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan phrase means social know-how, the practical knowledge of how to behave in any situation.

clue.text: Imitation white chocolate boxes

indicators.note: the words white chocolate box in, or contain, the letters we want

explanation.surface: A cheap copy of white chocolate sold in boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound repeats the original, so it is a copy, and figuratively any close imitation.

clue.text: Do like the trooper loveless boffin landed in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disordered, so they are rearranged
love is O in tennis scoring, and less means it is dropped

explanation.surface: A lonely scientist who has crash-landed behaves like a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' takes O from BOFFIN, leaving BFFIN; 'in trouble' rearranges that with LANDED. 'Swear like a trooper' is the idiom behind the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for swearing profusely, which a trooper proverbially does.

clue.text: A long meandering film about rustic, unlike Robert Browning?

indicators.note: a meandering course twists about, so these letters are rearranged
the film word goes around the rustic

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
a hob is a dialect word for a country bumpkin or rustic

explanation.surface: A lengthy rambling film about a country yokel, unlike the poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning wrote 'Home-Thoughts, from Abroad' ('Oh, to be in England'), so he was the opposite of someone who dislikes the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fears or dislikes England is unlike the poet, whose verse longs for it.

clue.text: Facilities for one undertaking madcap plan with ruler broken into 4

indicators.note: madcap means wild and reckless, so the following letters are thrown into a new order
the plan and ruler are smashed up together with the number word, all in one heap

parts.note: the setter wrote 'with a ruler' and the printed clue dropped the a, so the fodder here is a ruler
the figure in the clue is written out as the word four

explanation.surface: Someone launches a crazy scheme with a monarch, which is then split four ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue is one A short: the setter meant 'plan with a ruler', later corrected. 'madcap' and 'broken into' jumble PLAN, A RULER and the written-out 4 together.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker works from these premises, where bodies are prepared and mourners received.

clue.text: OK to run?

definitions.meaning: split as two words, a slang phrase meaning to run away

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer (3,2): British slang for to run off.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal for legitimate or allowed; its two halves also form slang for fleeing on foot.

clue.text: See 14
Governor's old title the old man has abandoned

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, the old man

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and uninhibited, so these letters run riot

explanation.surface: A father has given up a governor's old rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as a past-tense verb, but it is the adjective meaning unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the rank held by provincial governors and high officials in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Time to carve the contents of oven tin?

indicators.note: time cuts into, or carves, the next piece and sits inside it

parts.note: what is cooking in the oven is a meal

explanation.surface: A question at Sunday lunch: is it time to carve the roast in its tin?
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' does not pick out middle letters here; the oven's contents are the meal it cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is one example of a metal, hence the question mark marking a definition by example.

clue.text: Porter's absorbed by pivot

indicators.note: the beer takes the next piece inside itself

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an ale; the 's stands for has
the multiplication sign X is read as by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A railway porter is taken up by some central point of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is not a link: it is the times sign X, which the ale has absorbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod or spindle on which a wheel turns serves as its pivot.

clue.text: When I had trimmed land mass

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: trimmed means cut at both ends, leaving only the middle of the word had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the time they had a plot of land cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent is a land mass, a continent being a great expanse of land.

clue.text: Supple Miss Bott's telling us untruths?

indicators.note: Violet Elizabeth Bott speaks with a lisp, so we hear the word as she says it

parts.note: untruths are lies

explanation.surface: A girl called Miss Bott is supple, or perhaps she is fibbing to us.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott is the lisping girl in Richmal Crompton's Just William children's books, who threatens to 'thcream and thcream'; her lisp turns the S of LIES into TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym describing a body that bends easily and gracefully, as a dancer's does.

clue.text: See 4
See 6
One acquiring interest in shady Ted's occupation

indicators.note: shady suggests something dodgy and crooked, so these letters are twisted out of shape

parts.note: the letters of Ted's, including the S

explanation.surface: Someone takes an interest in what dodgy Ted does for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account where savings are left to earn interest is one thing that acquires it.

clue.text: See 22
Threateningly overhang weaving machine

definitions.meaning: to tower over in a menacing way, as storm clouds do
the frame on which yarn is woven into cloth

explanation.surface: A large weaving frame stands over a workshop in a menacing way.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to appear large and threatening; the noun is the apparatus for weaving thread into fabric.

clue.text: Restore Heads of School to English tech

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, taken from the next four

explanation.surface: School heads move to reinstate English at a technical college.
explanation.definitionFit: The proofreader's Latin mark meaning let it stand cancels a deletion, reinstating the text.

clue.text: Just touch pink, say — or pins, if ———-

definitions.meaning: to make the lightest contact, as billiard balls do
the word pink turns into pins when its ..., so the blank is filled by the answer split into three

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank puzzle about pinks and pins.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled by the answer split (1,2,1): if K is S, pink turns into pins.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards and snooker, balls that barely meet are said to make this light contact.

clue.text: False teeth finally accepted by American uncle

indicators.note: the uncle takes in the letter, which sits within his name

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word teeth

explanation.surface: An American uncle has been fitted with dentures.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence or fake, used as an adjective, means not genuine.

clue.text: Having rid oneself of slouch, correctly secure the stable door

definitions.meaning: sitting perfectly straight, with no slouch at all
fasten a door properly: shoot its bolt home and do it the right way

explanation.surface: Advice to sit up straight and to lock the stable properly before the horse escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as (4,2,5): to bolt (a door) up, and do it right.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sitting or standing rigidly erect, the opposite of slumping; split differently it reads as fastening something properly.

clue.text: Simplistic poem introduced by new article

indicators.note: the poem comes after the other pieces, which lead it in

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A short, simple poem printed after a fresh piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant of naive, borrowed from French, describing artless, unsophisticated thinking.

clue.text: Doctor on the mend, as there's more to give

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A recovering doctor still has more to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the patient's physician, but as a verb it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means and plenty more besides, used when there is still further to add.
